sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars, and I'm here with Emmett Fitzgerald, a 99PI producer, climate reporter, and as I've recently learned, a psychotic Arsenal fan.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯，今天和我在一起的是埃米特·菲茨杰拉德，他是《99%隐形》的制作人、气候记者，而且据我最近了解，他还是个疯狂的阿森纳球迷。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I've been mildly obsessed with the English football club Arsenal for basically my entire adult life.
sentences.zh: 我成年后的几乎整个生活里，都对英格兰足球俱乐部阿森纳有着轻微的痴迷。

sentences.en: To be clear, I have zero connection to North London where the team is based, but for reasons I can barely remember now, 14-year-old me chose Arsenal,
sentences.zh: 说清楚点，我和阿森纳所在的北伦敦没有任何联系，但出于我现在几乎记不清的原因，14岁那年的我选择了阿森纳，

sentences.en: and I've been living with the consequences ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我就一直承受着这个选择带来的后果。

sentences.en: You know, I wake up at like 6.30 in the morning basically every weekend to watch them play in Pacific Standard Time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每个周末我基本上都会在早上6点半起床，按照太平洋标准时间看他们比赛。

sentences.en: That's lunatic behavior, but okay.
sentences.zh: 那是疯子的行为，不过好吧。

sentences.en: It's nice to have a hobby.
sentences.zh: 有个爱好挺好的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, it's just my lot in life.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，这就是我的命。

sentences.en: But anyway, today is a big day because I have an Arsenal story for you.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，今天是个大日子，因为我有一个关于阿森纳的故事要讲给你听。

sentences.en: It starts with a match last season.
sentences.zh: 故事始于上赛季的一场比赛。

sentences.en: Arsenal were beating Bournemouth 2-0, and in the 52nd minute, Arsenal won a penalty.
sentences.zh: 当时阿森纳以2-0领先伯恩茅斯，在第52分钟，阿森纳获得了一个点球。

sentences.en: Now, normally in a situation like this, they would let their star player, this guy named Bakayo Saka, take the penalty kick.
sentences.zh: 通常在这种情况下，他们会让他们队里的明星球员，那个叫布卡约·萨卡的人来主罚点球。

sentences.en: But on this day, a lanky German named Kai Havertz stepped up.
sentences.zh: 但那天，一个叫凯·哈弗茨的瘦高个德国人站了出来。

sentences.en: They've given the ball to Kai Havertz.
sentences.zh: 他们把球交给了凯·哈弗茨。

sentences.en: So what's the significance of Kai Havertz and him taking the ball in this moment?
sentences.zh: 那么，凯·哈弗茨在这一刻接球有什么特殊意义吗？

sentences.en: So Kai Havertz had recently joined Arsenal from their London rivals, Chelsea, and he cost a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 凯·哈弗茨最近刚从他们的伦敦死敌切尔西转会到阿森纳，而且身价不菲。

sentences.en: He was a 60 million pound transfer.
sentences.zh: 他是一笔6000万英镑的转会。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But so far that season, he had still not scored a goal.
sentences.zh: 但那个赛季到目前为止，他还没进过球。

sentences.en: And the football media was starting to chatter about how all that money had been a waste.
sentences.zh: 足球媒体开始议论纷纷，说那笔钱全浪费了。

sentences.en: So, you know, Havertz is looking a little bit nervous as he approached the ball.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，哈弗茨走向皮球时看起来有点紧张。

sentences.en: But he smashed the penalty into the bottom left-hand corner.
sentences.zh: 但他还是把点球狠狠地轰进了球门左下角。

sentences.en: Now, this was not a particularly important goal in the season.
sentences.zh: 这并不是那个赛季中特别重要的一粒进球。

sentences.en: It wasn't really even an important goal in the game.
sentences.zh: 甚至在整场比赛中都算不上什么重要的进球。

sentences.en: You know, it was like already over, but it was an important goal for Kai Havertz.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比赛其实已经没悬念了，但这对凯·哈弗茨来说很重要。

sentences.en: And as he wheeled away into the corner to celebrate this, this, you know, first goal with the Arsenal fans, a song starts ringing around the stadium.
sentences.zh: 当他跑向角旗区庆祝这粒与阿森纳球迷共同打进的“首球”时，体育场内响起了一首歌。

sentences.en: Do you, do you, do you, does that mean anything to you to recognize that?
sentences.zh: 你，你，你，你听出来那是什么意思了吗？

sentences.en: It means nothing to me.
sentences.zh: 我完全听不出来。

sentences.en: Okay, so that, that is, that, if you did not, if you did not pick up on it, that is Shakira's 2010 hit, Waka Waka.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那是，那是，如果你没听出来的话，那是夏奇拉2010年的热门歌曲《Waka Waka》。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: So I do recognize that as the World Cup song, the, the, the World Cup in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 我确实认出那是世界杯的主题曲，南非世界杯的那首。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But instead of the usual Shakira verse, the Arsenal fans sang a brand new set of lyrics celebrating Kai Havertz and basically saying, who's a waste of money now?
sentences.zh: 但阿森纳球迷没有唱夏奇拉原本的歌词，而是唱了一套全新的歌词来赞美凯·哈弗茨，基本上是在说：现在谁才是浪费钱的那个？

sentences.en: 60 million down the drain, Kai Havertz scores a game.
sentences.zh: 六千万打了水漂，凯·哈弗茨进球了。

sentences.en: A reference to the price tag that was paid for Kai Havertz that was heavily criticized.
sentences.zh: 这是在调侃凯·哈弗茨那笔备受诟病的转会费。

sentences.en: And he does keep scoring.
sentences.zh: 而且他确实一直在进球。

sentences.en: This is James McNicholas.
sentences.zh: 这位是詹姆斯·麦克尼古拉斯。

sentences.en: Uh, I'm a sports writer.
sentences.zh: 呃，我是一名体育作家。

sentences.en: I work for The Athletic, where principally I cover Arsenal in the Premier League.
sentences.zh: 我为《竞技者》工作，主要负责报道英超联赛中的阿森纳。

sentences.en: And James says that on that day at Bournemouth, a new song was born.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯说，在伯恩茅斯的那一天，一首新歌诞生了。

sentences.en: And now, basically every time that Kai Havertz scores a goal, the fans start singing their version of this Shakira classic.
sentences.zh: 现在，基本上每次凯·哈弗茨进球，球迷们就会开始唱他们改编的这首夏奇拉经典歌曲。

sentences.en: Uh, I've got to say, I've got an 18-month-old son, uh, and that's certainly his favorite chant.
sentences.zh: 呃，我得说，我有个18个月大的儿子，那绝对是他最喜欢的助威歌。

sentences.en: Whenever that song comes on or whenever I'm singing that around the house, he really enjoys that.
sentences.zh: 每当那首歌响起，或者我在家里唱的时候，他都特别开心。

sentences.en: So I do have a particular soft spot for that one.
sentences.zh: 所以我对那首歌情有独钟。

sentences.en: And when he says that one, what he's implying here is that there are a lot of songs like the Waka Waka Kai Havertz song out there.
sentences.zh: 当他说“那首”的时候，他的意思是，像《Waka Waka》凯·哈弗茨之歌这样的歌曲还有很多。

sentences.en: There are so many songs like this in the English Premier League.
sentences.zh: 英超联赛里有太多这样的歌了。

sentences.en: There's no way I could possibly name them all.
sentences.zh: 我不可能把它们全列举出来。

sentences.en: But just to give you a quick taste of a couple of my favorites, Arsenal used to have this handsome French striker named Olivier Giroud.
sentences.zh: 但为了让你快速感受一下我最喜欢的几首，阿森纳曾经有一位帅气的法国前锋叫奥利维耶·吉鲁。

sentences.en: And the fans would sing his name to the tune of Hey Jude, as in, na-na-na-na, Giroud.
sentences.zh: 球迷们会用《Hey Jude》的旋律唱他的名字，就像这样：啦-啦-啦-啦，吉鲁。

sentences.en: One of my favorites of all time comes from West Ham, who had this song for their striker, Bobby Zamora,
sentences.zh: 我个人最喜欢的歌曲之一来自西汉姆联，他们为前锋鲍比·萨莫拉编过一首歌，

sentences.en: that was lovingly making fun of the fact that a lot of his shots tended to sail way above the goal.
sentences.zh: 那首歌充满爱意地调侃了他很多射门都高出横梁的事实。

sentences.en: Um, it was sung to the tune of That's Amore, except it went, when you're sat in Rosette and the ball hits your head, that's Zamora.
sentences.zh: 呃，它是用《That's Amore》的旋律唱的，歌词是：当你坐在罗塞特，球砸中你的头，那就是萨莫拉。

sentences.en: That's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 太精彩了。

sentences.en: That is truly just the tip of the iceberg.
sentences.zh: 那真的只是冰山一角。

sentences.en: If you have your TV unmuted while you watch an English Premier League game, you're treated to a near constant chorus of songs like these.
sentences.zh: 如果你在看英超比赛时没把电视静音，你就会听到几乎不间断的这类歌曲合唱。

sentences.en: I think it's partly what makes the Premier League so special.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是英超联赛如此特别的原因之一。

sentences.en: You know, these are songs with melodies borrowed from pop songs or folk songs and reworked lyrics, sometimes quite complex lyrics,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些歌曲的旋律借用了流行歌曲或民谣，并重新填了词，有时歌词还相当复杂，

sentences.en: which will be either to kind of eulogize their own players, lionize their own players, or are often quite derogatory about other players and other teaMs.
sentences.zh: 要么是为了赞美、推崇他们自己的球员，要么通常是对其他球员和其他球队进行相当刻薄的讽刺。

sentences.en: But the imagination and sense of humor of the British football fan knows few bounds.
sentences.zh: 但英国足球迷的想象力和幽默感是无止境的。

sentences.en: And, you know, this obviously isn't unique to English soccer.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这显然不是英格兰足球独有的。

sentences.en: Football fans all over the world sing during matches.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的足球迷在比赛时都会唱歌。

sentences.en: And even American sports fans have some simple chants that they break out now and then.
sentences.zh: 即使是美国体育迷偶尔也会喊一些简单的口号。

sentences.en: But I think English soccer singing has become almost like a folk art form.
sentences.zh: 但我认为英格兰足球的歌唱已经变成了一种民间艺术形式。

sentences.en: The songs have complicated melodies and clever lyrics.
sentences.zh: 这些歌曲有着复杂的旋律和巧妙的歌词。

sentences.en: And each team has an entirely unique songbook that seemingly every fan in the stadium knows by heart.
sentences.zh: 每支球队都有一个完全独特的歌集，体育场里的每个球迷似乎都烂熟于心。

sentences.en: And I have to say, watching on TV from California, I've always been both mesmerized and confused by this whole phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 我必须得说，在加利福尼亚看电视转播时，我一直对这种现象既着迷又困惑。

sentences.en: Like, every time I watched an Arsenal game, it felt like there was a new song that didn't even exist the previous match.
sentences.zh: 就像每次我看阿森纳比赛时，感觉总有一首上一场比赛还没出现过的新歌。

sentences.en: And somehow, 40,000 fans just seemed to know exactly how and when to sing it.
sentences.zh: 而且不知何故，四万名球迷似乎都知道该怎么唱、什么时候唱。

sentences.en: And so I went on a journey into the history of football fan culture and pop music to try and figure out how all this actually works.
sentences.zh: 所以我踏上了一段探索足球球迷文化和流行音乐历史的旅程，试图弄清楚这一切到底是如何运作的。

sentences.en: And who is even writing these songs that are perpetually bouncing around in my head?
sentences.zh: 还有，到底是谁在写这些在我脑海里不断回响的歌？

sentences.en: Okay, so where do you begin with this?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那从哪里开始讲起呢？

sentences.en: Let's start with the football writer, Andy Lawn.
sentences.zh: 让我们从足球作家安迪·劳恩开始吧。

sentences.en: I have always been fascinated by football crowds or soccer crowds and just the noise that they make.
sentences.zh: 我一直对足球观众或者说球迷群体，以及他们制造出的那种噪音非常着迷。

sentences.en: Andy is the author of We Lose Every Week, a history of football chanting.
sentences.zh: 安迪是《我们每周都输》的作者，这是一本关于足球助威歌历史的书。

sentences.en: And he says that part of why he wanted to write the book in the first place is that singing soccer fans tend to get a pretty bad rap.
sentences.zh: 他说，他最初想写这本书的部分原因，是因为唱歌的足球迷往往名声不太好。

sentences.en: I knew that a lot of the discourse around soccer fandom focused on hooliganism.
sentences.zh: 我知道很多关于足球迷的讨论都集中在足球流氓行为上。

sentences.en: A lot of the kind of times that football chanting made the news it was for racism or for homophobia or for some really like dark, abusive, horrible stuff.
sentences.zh: 很多时候足球助威歌上新闻，都是因为种族歧视、恐同，或者是一些非常阴暗、辱骂、可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Andy says that that part of football culture is unfortunately very real.
sentences.zh: 安迪说，足球文化中的那一部分不幸的是非常真实的。

sentences.en: But he also knew from a lifetime of experience inside football grounds that it wasn't the full story.
sentences.zh: 但他从一生在足球场内的经历中也知道，那并不是全部事实。

sentences.en: Because I knew that chanting and singing and that kind of communal experience was much more than hooliganism.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道助威、唱歌以及那种集体体验远不止是流氓行为。

sentences.en: It was a way to express kind of civic pride and identity in something that you kind of really believed in.
sentences.zh: 这是一种表达公民自豪感和对某种你真正信仰的事物产生认同感的方式。

sentences.en: And I didn't think that that story was widely enough known.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得那个故事并没有被足够广泛地了解。

sentences.en: In his book, Andy traces the origins of football chants back to his own hometown of Norwich in the late 19th century.
sentences.zh: 在书中，安迪将足球助威歌的起源追溯到了他家乡诺里奇的19世纪末。

sentences.en: And back then, most cities had a bunch of different football clubs that were mostly connected to local employers.
sentences.zh: 那时，大多数城市都有许多不同的足球俱乐部，它们大多与当地的雇主有关。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you've ever wondered where Arsenal got its name, the team was originally made up of workers from a munitions factory.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果你曾经好奇阿森纳的名字是怎么来的，这支球队最初是由一家军工厂的工人组成的。

sentences.en: Oh, I actually didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我其实不知道这一点。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: And in Norwich, where Andy was from, there were like six or seven different teaMs.
sentences.zh: 在安迪家乡诺里奇，有六七支不同的球队。

sentences.en: So, there was a team that was made up of employees from the Cayley's Chocolate Factory.
sentences.zh: 有一支球队是由凯利巧克力工厂的员工组成的。

sentences.en: There was a team made up of teachers.
sentences.zh: 有一支球队是由教师组成的。

sentences.en: There was a team made up of people from the local church.
sentences.zh: 有一支球队是由当地教堂的人组成的。

sentences.en: And they would play against each other in a kind of hyper-local league.
sentences.zh: 他们会在一种超本地化的联赛中互相比赛。

sentences.en: In the 1890s, a local Norwich man wrote a song called On The Ball City, celebrating the fact that Norwich had so many football teaMs.
sentences.zh: 19世纪90年代，一位诺里奇当地人写了一首名为《球场上的城市》的歌，庆祝诺里奇拥有这么多足球队。

sentences.en: And then a few years later, when those teams eventually merged to create Norwich City FC, they basically started singing that song as like an anthem for the new combined team.
sentences.zh: 几年后，当这些球队最终合并创建诺里奇城足球俱乐部时，他们基本上就开始唱那首歌作为新合并球队的队歌了。

sentences.en: And it just became a tradition that kind of caught on.
sentences.zh: 这成了一种流行的传统。

sentences.en: And that was in 1902.
sentences.zh: 那是1902年的事了。

sentences.en: Now in 2025, it's still being sung by every game four or five times in a game.
sentences.zh: 现在是2025年，每场比赛他们还在唱，一场比赛要唱四五次。

sentences.en: Okay, so most people consider On The Ball City to be the first football song.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以大多数人认为《球场上的城市》是第一首足球歌曲。

sentences.en: But soon, fans of other teams followed suit and started singing songs meant to celebrate local pride.
sentences.zh: 但很快，其他球队的球迷也纷纷效仿，开始唱起旨在庆祝当地自豪感的歌曲。

sentences.en: So, for example, supporters of Portsmouth Football Club, which is nicknamed Pompey, started singing a song called Play Up Pompey.
sentences.zh: 例如，朴茨茅斯足球俱乐部的支持者（绰号“庞培”）开始唱一首名为《加油庞培》的歌。

sentences.en: Which is a chant that's very simple.
sentences.zh: 那是一首非常简单的助威歌。

sentences.en: It's a bit more like a kind of a U.S.
sentences.zh: 它更像是一种美国式的

sentences.en: chant.
sentences.zh: 助威口号。

sentences.en: It's simply just play up Pompey, Pompey, play up, play up Pompey.
sentences.zh: 它仅仅就是：加油庞培，庞培，加油，加油庞培。

sentences.en: But the way they sing it chimed perfectly with the town hall bells that was next to the stadium.
sentences.zh: 但他们唱的方式与体育场旁边的市政厅钟声完美契合。

sentences.en: So it's that da-da-da-da, da-da-da-da.
sentences.zh: 所以就是那种哒-哒-哒-哒，哒-哒-哒-哒。

sentences.en: So you mentioned the first one sort of premiered around 1902.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到第一首歌大约是在1902年首唱的。

sentences.en: You know, where are we at this point where they start spreading around to other clubs?
sentences.zh: 你知道，在他们开始传播到其他俱乐部时，我们处于什么阶段？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, kind of the early part of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，那是20世纪初的早期阶段。

sentences.en: It was this like, it was a phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种现象。

sentences.en: But, you know, different teams would have them.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，不同的球队会有不同的歌。

sentences.en: They were often sung at the beginnings of games.
sentences.zh: 它们通常在比赛开始时唱。

sentences.en: Like, before anything even happened, it was kind of like the players are walking out onto the field.
sentences.zh: 就像在任何事情发生之前，球员们正走上球场时那样。

sentences.en: Like, let's sing the song from our town that celebrates local pride.
sentences.zh: 就像是：让我们唱起我们城镇的歌，庆祝当地的自豪感。

sentences.en: But I would say that, like, if we're going to call football songwriting a folk art form, as I did in the intro,
sentences.zh: 但我会说，如果我们要把足球歌曲创作称为一种民间艺术形式，正如我在开场白中所说的那样，

sentences.en: So I would say that, like, that didn't really kick into gear until the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 我会说，直到20世纪60年代，它才真正开始进入状态。

sentences.en: And it all went down in Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生在利物浦。

sentences.en: And what essentially happened was Cilla Black and the Beatles were kind of the first musical acts that became world famous.
sentences.zh: 本质上发生的事情是，西拉·布莱克和披头士乐队是第一批享誉世界的音乐艺人。

sentences.en: And they were very, very famously from Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 而且他们非常非常出名地来自利物浦。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, Liverpool also had one of the best football teams in the league, really in Europe, Liverpool FC.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，利物浦也拥有联赛中，甚至是欧洲最好的足球队之一，利物浦足球俱乐部。

sentences.en: And it kind of, you know, it just kind of made sense that these two things would collide.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这两件事碰撞在一起是很自然的事。

sentences.en: So the Liverpool crowd used their songs as a vehicle for kind of pride and self-identity.
sentences.zh: 因此，利物浦的观众把他们的歌曲作为一种自豪感和自我认同的载体。

sentences.en: Because here are these people who are a global success, the first kind of global superstars that certainly England has produced.
sentences.zh: 因为这些人是全球性的成功者，是英格兰所产生的首批全球超级巨星。

sentences.en: And they're from Liverpool and they sound like us.
sentences.zh: 他们来自利物浦，听起来和我们一样。

sentences.en: And so Liverpool fans just started singing Beatles songs verbatim during home matches at their famously loud stadium, which is called Anfield.
sentences.zh: 于是利物浦球迷开始在主场比赛时，在他们以喧闹著称的安菲尔德球场，一字不差地唱起披头士的歌。

sentences.en: Here is a clip from 1964 of the raucous Anfield crowd singing She Loves You by the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 这是一段1964年安菲尔德喧闹的观众唱披头士《她爱你》的片段。

sentences.en: But the most iconic Liverpool song from this area isn't actually a Beatles song.
sentences.zh: 但那个时期最标志性的利物浦歌曲其实并不是披头士的歌。

sentences.en: It's called You'll Never Walk Alone.
sentences.zh: 它叫《你永远不会独行》。

sentences.en: Do you know that song?
sentences.zh: 你知道那首歌吗？

sentences.en: I know it, but I really only know it in this context.
sentences.zh: 我知道，但我真的只在这个语境下知道它。

sentences.en: I don't know where it originates from.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它起源于哪里。

sentences.en: Well, it was originally written for a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它最初是为罗杰斯与汉默斯坦的音乐剧创作的。

sentences.en: But the song was made famous by a Liverpool rock band called Jerry and the Pacemakers.
sentences.zh: 但这首歌是由一支叫“杰里与领跑者”的利物浦摇滚乐队唱红的。

sentences.en: It's not exactly a jock jam.
sentences.zh: 它算不上那种运动场上的劲歌。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Okay, yes, but listen to the Liverpool crowd sing it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是的，但听听利物浦观众唱它。

sentences.en: Oh, it's so good.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: You would never predict that for that song, but it actually comes off so well.
sentences.zh: 你永远不会预料到那首歌会这样，但它唱出来效果真的很好。

sentences.en: Totally, totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意，完全同意。

sentences.en: And that has become Liverpool's anthem that's known all around the world.
sentences.zh: 那已经成为了利物浦的队歌，全世界都知道。

sentences.en: If you tell someone you're a Liverpool fan, they'll start singing.
sentences.zh: 如果你告诉别人你是利物浦球迷，他们就会开始唱歌。

sentences.en: They'll never walk alone at you in an airport.
sentences.zh: 在机场他们就会对着你唱《你永远不会独行》。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it wasn't long before other clubs started taking notice of what was going on in Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，没过多久其他俱乐部就开始注意到利物浦发生的事情了。

sentences.en: Teams, you know, from all over the country would come to Anfield.
sentences.zh: 来自全国各地的球队都会来到安菲尔德。

sentences.en: And when their fans arrived, you know, not only is this team, this Liverpool team, one of the best teams we've ever played against,
sentences.zh: 当他们的球迷到达时，你知道，不仅这支利物浦队是我们交手过的最好的球队之一，

sentences.en: but there are rows and rows of these crazy Liverpool fans just like singing Beatles songs at the top of their lungs.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一排排疯狂的利物浦球迷在声嘶力竭地唱着披头士的歌。

sentences.en: And fans kind of took that inspiration, like, these guys are singing pop songs, and they're really loud, and it's a really fun environment, and their team are winning.
sentences.zh: 球迷们从中获得了灵感，就像是：这些人唱着流行歌曲，他们声音很大，环境非常有趣，而且他们的球队还在赢球。

sentences.en: We can do that at home.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在家里那样做。

sentences.en: I mean, that's all fine and good, but not every town has a Beatles in their back pocket.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这固然很好，但并不是每个城镇都能随手掏出一个披头士乐队。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: Right, I mean, like, good luck singing all the world-famous songs from all the bands in Wolverhampton, or Bournemouth, or Norwich, for that matter.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，祝你在伍尔弗汉普顿、伯恩茅斯或诺里奇唱出所有那些世界名曲，或者说，随便哪个地方都行。

sentences.en: We don't necessarily have an artist that is from Norwich who is world-famous, so what can we do?
sentences.zh: 我们不一定有来自诺里奇的世界级明星，那我们能做什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, we can maybe change the words of the song, so we can have the same tune.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许我们可以改改歌词，这样就能用同样的曲调了。

sentences.en: Everyone knows this tune.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道这个曲调。

sentences.en: No one needs to learn the tune.
sentences.zh: 没人需要去学这首歌的旋律。

sentences.en: Everyone knows this tune.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道这个曲调。

sentences.en: We can just sing it, but we can change it and make it our own words.
sentences.zh: 我们可以直接唱，但可以改动一下，填上我们自己的歌词。

sentences.en: So this is the moment when fans start making their own football-specific remixes,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是球迷开始制作专属足球混音版的时候，

sentences.en: taking well-known pop melodies and writing their own lyrics to suit their particular city or their football club.
sentences.zh: 他们采用广为人知的流行旋律，写下属于自己城市或足球俱乐部的歌词。

sentences.en: So the song itself isn't from a particular city, but now it has new lyrics that might be about how great Norwich is, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以这首歌本身并不属于某个特定城市，但现在它有了新的歌词，可能是在赞美诺里奇有多棒，或者诸如此类的内容。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Or how good their team is on the pitch.
sentences.zh: 或者赞美他们的球队在场上表现有多好。

sentences.en: You know, for example, in the case of Arsenal, the fans wrote a classic song celebrating how tough the team's defense was.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如阿森纳的例子，球迷们写了一首经典歌曲，赞美球队的防守有多强悍。

sentences.en: One which sort of came out of the late 80s, early 90s is 1-0 to the Arsenal, which I believe is to the tune of Go West by the Pet Shop Boys.
sentences.zh: 其中一首大概是在80年代末、90年代初出现的，叫《1-0 to the Arsenal》（阿森纳1-0），我相信它的曲调来自宠物店男孩乐队的《Go West》。

sentences.en: And that became kind of the quintessential Arsenal chant.
sentences.zh: 那首歌成了阿森纳最具代表性的助威歌。

sentences.en: And the reason I love it is because 1-0, I mean, I'm sure your American listeners will turn up their noses at a scoreline as dour as that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它的原因在于，1-0，我的意思是，我相信你们的美国听众会对如此沉闷的比分嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: That's the problem with soccer, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是足球的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Not enough goals.
sentences.zh: 进球不够多。

sentences.en: And back in the 90s, Arsenal was getting criticized, you know, essentially for being boring to watch because they won so many of their games 1-0.
sentences.zh: 而在90年代，阿森纳受到了批评，你知道，本质上是因为他们赢下那么多比赛都是1-0，看起来很无聊。

sentences.en: And Arsenal fans, being what they are, you know, they turned that into a positive and they dug their heels in and were proud of that identity.
sentences.zh: 而阿森纳球迷，毕竟是阿森纳球迷，你知道，他们把这变成了一种积极的东西，他们坚持己见，并为这种身份感到自豪。

sentences.en: They were going to be the meanest, nastiest, toughest to break down team in the league and celebrate every one of those 1-0 to the Arsenal wins.
sentences.zh: 他们要成为联赛中最刻薄、最讨厌、最难被攻破的球队，并庆祝每一次“阿森纳1-0”的胜利。

sentences.en: And they did that through songs.
sentences.zh: 他们通过歌曲做到了这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Can we get a few bars?
sentences.zh: 能来几句吗？

sentences.en: I've heard you sing on a podcast before.
sentences.zh: 我以前在播客上听你唱过。

sentences.en: Okay, I will give you a, I'll give you a blaSt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我给你来一段，我给你露一手。

sentences.en: So obviously it's 1-0 to the Arsenal, 1-0 to the Arsenal, 1-0.
sentences.zh: 显然就是“1-0 to the Arsenal, 1-0 to the Arsenal, 1-0”。

sentences.en: Listen, lyrically, it's not the most complex, but you can see why it courts on.
sentences.zh: 听着，从歌词上讲，它不是最复杂的，但你可以看出为什么它能流行起来。

sentences.en: I mean, it's still a farsight better than just defense.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它总比只喊“防守”要好得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, simplicity was key back then.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那时候简单就是关键。

sentences.en: There was, you know, there's no internet, no social media.
sentences.zh: 那时候没有互联网，没有社交媒体。

sentences.en: These songs needed to go viral in the real world.
sentences.zh: 这些歌需要在现实世界中传播开来。

sentences.en: And you can kind of imagine how this might play out.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下这是怎么发生的。

sentences.en: Like if you were a diehard fan in the stadium, you would basically need to sing your new song loudly enough and clearly enough that the drunk guys next to you would pick it up.
sentences.zh: 比如如果你是体育场里的铁杆球迷，你基本上需要足够大声、足够清晰地唱出你的新歌，这样你旁边的醉汉才会跟着唱。

sentences.en: And then hope that they sang it loudly enough and clearly enough that the drunk fans next to them caught on.
sentences.zh: 然后希望他们能足够大声、足够清晰地唱出来，让旁边的醉酒球迷也学会。

sentences.en: They don't hand out a song sheet or anything, you know, there's not a hymn book, right?
sentences.zh: 他们不会分发歌单什么的，你知道，又没有赞美诗集，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to go away and ask your mates, what do they actually sing?
sentences.zh: 你得去问你的朋友，他们到底唱的是什么？

sentences.en: What are the words there?
sentences.zh: 那里的歌词是什么？

sentences.en: Or just come back enough times that you slowly pick it up.
sentences.zh: 或者多来几次，慢慢地就学会了。

sentences.en: I mean, given that, it's kind of amazing that any songs got learned at all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，考虑到这一点，任何歌曲能被学会都挺神奇的。

sentences.en: Totally, totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意，完全同意。

sentences.en: But over time, this kind of clever pop music songwriting really spread all throughout football.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，这种巧妙的流行音乐创作方式确实在整个足球界传播开来。

sentences.en: And because these songs were sung during the game itself, it made the relationship between the crowd and what was happening on the field so much more dynamic.
sentences.zh: 而且因为这些歌是在比赛中唱的，它使得观众与场上发生的事情之间的关系变得更加动态。

sentences.en: Yeah, there is that kind of symbioticism between the crowd and the players.
sentences.zh: 是的，观众和球员之间确实存在那种共生关系。

sentences.en: And sometimes they feed each other.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会互相激励。

sentences.en: You know, it might be that the team is struggling.
sentences.zh: 你知道，可能是球队陷入困境时。

sentences.en: It might be that they need picking up and maybe an anthemic song could be what lifts them, what rouses them.
sentences.zh: 可能是他们需要振作起来，也许一首赞歌就能激励他们，唤醒他们。

sentences.en: Or when a team's scored, the fans might start singing a song devoted specifically to the player who got the goal.
sentences.zh: 或者当球队进球时，球迷可能会开始唱一首专门献给进球球员的歌。

sentences.en: So, for example, in the late 90s, early 2000s, Arsenal had this legendary midfielder named Patrick Vieira.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如在90年代末、2000年代初，阿森纳有一位传奇中场叫帕特里克·维埃拉。

sentences.en: He was French, but he was born in Senegal.
sentences.zh: 他是法国人，但出生在塞内加尔。

sentences.en: And he had a chant to the tune of, I believe the song's called Valare, which was, I'll sing it for you.
sentences.zh: 他有一首助威歌，曲调我记得叫《Valare》，是这样的，我给你唱一下。

sentences.en: It went, Vieira, whoa, Vieira, whoa, he comes from Senegal, he plays for Arsenal.
sentences.zh: 歌词是：维埃拉，喔，维埃拉，喔，他来自塞内加尔，他为阿森纳效力。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: But I take it not every player warrants a special song.
sentences.zh: 但我猜并不是每个球员都能有专属歌曲。

sentences.en: Oh, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，不，不。

sentences.en: It's something, it's something that, you know, it's something that you have to earn.
sentences.zh: 这是某种，这是某种，你知道，这是某种你必须赢得的东西。

sentences.en: The moment where you get your own song from your fans is like when you've arrived, you know, and I think it takes some time.
sentences.zh: 当你从球迷那里得到专属歌曲的那一刻，就像是你功成名就了，你知道，我认为这需要一些时间。

sentences.en: You know, the stadium lyricists have to go away, squirrel away and come up with something and then it's got to catch on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，体育场的作词家们必须去钻研，去构思，然后它还得流行起来。

sentences.en: But that, it must be a wonderful moment for a player.
sentences.zh: 但那对球员来说一定是一个美妙的时刻。

sentences.en: And it's something players often talk about.
sentences.zh: 这也是球员们经常谈论的事情。

sentences.en: You know, I heard the fans seeing my name for the first time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我第一次听到球迷唱我的名字。

sentences.en: One thing that has consistently baffled me about the chants that I hear on TV every weekend is the fact that these songs just seem to pop out of thin air.
sentences.zh: 有一件事一直让我对每个周末在电视上听到的助威歌感到困惑，那就是这些歌似乎是凭空冒出来的。

sentences.en: One week, a song doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 这一周，这首歌还不存在。

sentences.en: And the next, tens of thousands of people are screaming it in unison.
sentences.zh: 下一周，成千上万的人就在齐声高唱了。

sentences.en: So after the break, I will talk with one of the songwriting supporters who make that magic happen.
sentences.zh: 所以休息之后，我将与一位促成这种魔力的歌曲创作支持者谈谈。

sentences.en: All right, stay tuned.
sentences.zh: 好的，请继续收听。

sentences.en: Okay, we are back with Emmett to try to understand the origins of soccer songs.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们回来继续和埃米特探讨足球歌曲的起源。

sentences.en: So since I started reporting this piece,
sentences.zh: 所以自从我开始报道这个专题以来，

sentences.en: I've wanted to try and figure out who was actually writing all of these songs that seemed to spring forth from the chaos of the crowd like magic.
sentences.zh: 我就一直想弄清楚，到底是谁在写所有这些似乎像魔法一样从混乱的观众席中涌现出来的歌曲。

sentences.en: And that search led me to an Arsenal fan named Dan Gunning.
sentences.zh: 而那次搜索让我找到了一个叫丹·甘宁的阿森纳球迷。

sentences.en: It started because as a group, we wanted to try and improve the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 这一切的开始是因为作为一个群体，我们想尝试改善现场气氛。

sentences.en: It's circular, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个循环，对吧？

sentences.en: The fans sing more, it helps the players.
sentences.zh: 球迷唱得越多，就越能帮助球员。

sentences.en: The players win, the players win.
sentences.zh: 球员赢球，球员赢球。

sentences.en: The fans sing more, it goes round and round.
sentences.zh: 球迷唱得更多，周而复始。

sentences.en: Dan is a season ticket holder in this very famous part of the stadium called the North Bank.
sentences.zh: 丹是体育场一个非常著名的区域——北岸看台的季票持有者。

sentences.en: And, you know, he's a regular at Arsenal Games.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他是阿森纳比赛的常客。

sentences.en: And, you know, it must be said that Arsenal have never been known for being a particularly rowdy crowd.
sentences.zh: 而且，必须说的是，阿森纳从来没有以吵闹的球迷群体而闻名。

sentences.en: They're not Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 他们不是利物浦。

sentences.en: But when fans were let back into the stadium after COVID, Arsenal was playing really well.
sentences.zh: 但在新冠疫情后球迷被允许回到体育场时，阿森纳踢得非常好。

sentences.en: And there was this concerted effort to try and improve the atmosphere inside the ground.
sentences.zh: 于是大家齐心协力，试图改善场内的气氛。

sentences.en: Try and really create, you know, a vibe inside that stadium.
sentences.zh: 试图在体育场内真正营造出一种氛围。

sentences.en: Dan and his friends were a part of that.
sentences.zh: 丹和他的朋友们就是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And they decided to take it upon themselves to write some fresh songs for some of the team's newest players.
sentences.zh: 他们决定自己动手，为球队的一些新球员写一些新歌。

sentences.en: We started to get some noise from fans saying, you know, well, this person needs a song or that person needs a song.
sentences.zh: 我们开始听到球迷们说，你知道，这个人需要一首歌，或者那个人需要一首歌。

sentences.en: Specifically, Dan thought that the team really desperately needed a song for their new captain, who is a Norwegian midfielder named Martin Odegaard.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，丹认为球队非常迫切地需要为他们的新队长——一位名叫马丁·厄德高的挪威中场——写一首歌。

sentences.en: Odegaard is this incredibly skilled kind of baby-faced Scandinavian who wears the number eight jersey.
sentences.zh: 厄德高是一个技术极其精湛、长着一张娃娃脸的斯堪的纳维亚人，身穿8号球衣。

sentences.en: Wait, so he's saying watching darts, like watching people throw darts on YouTube?
sentences.zh: 等等，所以他说的是看飞镖，就像在YouTube上看人们投飞镖吗？

sentences.en: Is that what he's watching?
sentences.zh: 他看的是那个吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, he did.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对，他确实看了。

sentences.en: You know, darts is like a popular spectator sport and they televise it in the UK.
sentences.zh: 你知道，飞镖是一项受欢迎的观赏性运动，英国有电视转播。

sentences.en: And the theme song for the main darts television program is by a band called Planet Funk.
sentences.zh: 而主要的飞镖电视节目的主题曲是由一个叫Planet Funk的乐队创作的。

sentences.en: It's called Chase the Sun.
sentences.zh: 它叫《Chase the Sun》。

sentences.en: And then I put in the group chat and said, what do you guys think about a football song for this?
sentences.zh: 然后我发到群聊里说，你们觉得用这个做足球歌曲怎么样？

sentences.en: It was a very astute choice because that song has a particular resonance in North London, I would say,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常敏锐的选择，因为那首歌在北伦敦有一种特殊的共鸣，我想说，

sentences.en: even because every year there's the big darts competition here at Alexandra Palace, which is only about 20 minutes from the stadium.
